title: Nonlinearity above one third for APN and 4-uniform permutations
summary: Determine whether every APN or differentially 4-uniform binary permutation without affine components has nonlinearity strictly greater than one third of the code-space size.

formal_statement.body: For every integer $m\ge 6$ and every permutation $F:\mathbb F_{2^m}\to\mathbb F_{2^m}$ without affine components whose differential uniformity is in $\{2,4\}$, is $\operatorname{NL}(F)>2^m/3$? Prove the universal inequality or give an admissible counterexample with $\operatorname{NL}(F)\le 2^m/3$.

scope.domain: APN and differentially 4-uniform permutations over binary finite fields
assumptions: m is an integer with m >= 6
F is a permutation of F_(2^m)
The differential uniformity of F is 2 or 4
scope.unresolved_remainder: The threshold is proved for the later infinite Welch 4-uniform permutation family in odd dimensions at least seven. It remains open for every admissible APN permutation and for all other admissible 4-uniform permutations in the source range.

progress.summary: The source asks whether the one-third nonlinearity threshold holds universally over the stated APN and 4-uniform permutation classes for m at least six.
A later paper proves the threshold for an infinite family of differentially 4-uniform Welch permutations in every odd dimension at least seven.
